slides.title: A first look at your Seestar measurements.
slides.body: Import target CSVs, a field folder or a completed MyWorks collection. Add observations in either order, then explore what deserves a closer look.
slides.note: Free, browser-local and read-only. Every measurement in these screenshots is fictional; no private observing data is shown.

slides.title: One object. Its source runs.
slides.body: Choose an object and the runs to include. Inspect target/field overlap before combining observations: this example keeps 180 measurements and excludes 180 duplicate exports.
slides.note: Two exports of the same observation are not independent confirmation. Coordinate associations are provisional; different-night brightness offsets are not automatically corrected.

slides.title: View all your miniature curves.
slides.body: Browse every curve matching the gallery filters. Choose tile size and scale, then sort by review priority, coverage or range to decide what to inspect.
slides.note: These 24 fictional objects contain invented dips, waves and trends. Review priority is a browsing aid, not an eclipse probability or a complete search for events.

slides.title: Open the curve behind a thumbnail.
slides.body: Select a miniature to inspect its measurements and binned trend. The gallery can close automatically; Back to gallery returns to the highlighted tile.
slides.note: Check gaps, uncertainty and tracking before interpreting a shape. An interesting curve can reflect a real change, noise or the measurement process.

slides.title: See what a cutoff will remove.
slides.body: Bar height counts measurements. SNR and uncertainty sliders span the loaded range; striped portions show which values fail each cutoff. Enable Hide flagged measurements to see the filtered curve.
slides.note: Here SNR flags 58 and uncertainty flags 55, with 55 in both groups: 58 unique flags, leaving 122 of 180 measurements. Uncertainty is measurement error, not brightness. Gallery thumbnails remain unfiltered.

slides.title: Mark a question worth following up.
slides.body: Mark an object beside its main chart, selector or gallery tile. Add a review note; the controls share the same shortlist so you can move between views.
slides.note: Marks mean “investigate further”, not “confirmed variable”. Download notes and provenance before refreshing; they do not restore a complete workspace.

slides.title: Take selected observations into VStar.
slides.body: Export the current object and included runs. The optional quality switch applies your cutoffs to individual measurements. Open the downloaded text file in VStar using its simple-format reader.
slides.note: This capture produced a 122-row download with original start JD, magnitude and uncertainty. Ordinary and filtered exports are tested in VStar 2.25.0 on macOS. No passband calibration or AAVSO submission is implied.

slides.title: Triage here. Analyse further when needed.
slides.body: Setup groups optional ASTAP catalogue access, VStar guidance and remembered folders. Use VStar for deeper time-series work, or take the original FITS exposures to a dedicated tool for independent photometry.
slides.note: FITS remeasurement needs image pixels, calibration and comparison-star choices. This analyzer explores exported measurements; it does not perform FITS photometry or automatically confirm discoveries.
